text: Getting started with doeff: algebraic effects for Python.
A program yields an effect. A handler gets it, together with k: the rest of the program.
What the handler does with k decides what the effect means: resume it, throw into it, pass it on, or drop it.
Your first program, counter program, yields Put, Tell, and Get.
Each effect goes out to the handler that answers it: state for Get and Put, writer for Tell.
Each answer comes back to its yield, and the code goes on. The run returns one.
Now your first effect of your own: Progress, a frozen dataclass under EffectBase.
shrink all yields Progress after each image. What that report means is up to a handler.
The show handler notes each Progress and resumes k. All three images are shrunk.
stop after two returns at the second report, without resuming k.
So the rest is dropped, and the third image is never shrunk. Same program, another meaning.
Handlers can start with values: reader with an environment, and state with an initial state.
Ask is answered from the environment, and Get from the initial state.
Start state with another user id, and the same program connects as user seven.
Programs yield effects, and handlers decide what they mean. Core Concepts lists everything a handler can do. pip install doeff.
